title: Rebaseline Console MVP: mini-insight portfolio cuts, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Background: The Console observability surface has grown beyond the resourcing envelope for the March MVP. Multiple dashboard cards, deep trace sampling, and a full route-level cost explorer are high value but high cost to implement. This ticket captures a pragmatic rebaseline: a compact 'mini-insight portfolio' that preserves core value for platform users (engineers and platform teams) while trimming implementation scope to meet the release date.

Goals:
- Deliver a minimal yet actionable Console that helps engineers triage latency, error spikes, and surprising cost drivers at route/model granularity.
- Keep implementation work within current sprint capacity and avoid high-risk infra changes.
- Provide clear acceptance criteria and rollout plan so downstream teams (support, docs, Solutions) can prepare.

Scope decisions (what we will ship in MVP):
1) Essential route cards (2): latency median/P95 and token cost delta for top 10 routes. Lightweight aggregation only (no per-token breakdown).
2) Compact trace view: show a sampled single-request flamegraph and error annotations; no full distributed tracing UI, limit to top 3 services.
3) Cost spotlight: weekly delta card + top-3 anomaly reasons surfaced (model switch, traffic spike, quantization change). No per-route drilldown in MVP.
4) Rollouts & alerts: basic A/B rollout dashboard and anomaly EMAIL alerts for cost deltas. No in-console alerting config for MVP.

Out-of-scope (cut for MVP):
- Full trace exploration with span timeline scrubbing and custom sampling rules.
- Token-level cost explorer and per-token timeline charts.
- Unlimited per-organization retention tiers and historical comparison beyond 30 days.
- Self-serve sampling policy editor in Console.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- We favor breadth of signal over depth: provide quick surface-level signals to unblock incident response and cost investigations, while deferring heavy UX and infra work for subsequent releases.
- Avoid implementing custom long-term storage for traces in MVP to reduce infra risk; leverage sampling + short retention.
- Some users will lose fine-grained controls, but will retain visibility into the most common failure/cost patterns.

Acceptance criteria (must all be met for this ticket to be Done):
- Route cards: show top 10 routes by request volume with median latency and P95 for the last 1h/24h windows; values refresh within established telemetry SLA (<=60s).
- Cost spotlight card: displays weekly cost delta and attributes top-3 reasons (categorical) with links to the source usage records.
- Compact trace: for simulated error traces (test harness), Console displays a sampled flamegraph, marks error spans, and links to the raw trace ID.
- Rollout dashboard: can display split percentages for active rollouts and surface the active canary route in the UI.
- Alerts: email notifications are triggered for cost deltas >20% on production routes and include a link to the Console card.
- Docs: product docs and release notes updated with MVP limitations and migration path to full features.
- Performance: added UI components respond within 300ms on staging with production-like data sampling; backend telemetry queries meet 60s SLO.
- Security & privacy: no customer PII is shown in trace snippets; retention policy for traces is set to 30 days for MVP.

Monitoring & telemetry for rollout:
- Dashboard to track card load success rate, average telemetry query duration, trace sampling ratio, and email alert delivery rate.
- Burn-in checklist: 72 hours of stable telemetry (no more than 5% error rate on card loads) before enabling rollout to Tier-1 customers.

Implementation notes & links:
- PRD draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/R-INF/Console+Mini-Insight+Portfolio+PRD (doc contains mockups and data contracts).
- Design mocks: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/mini-insight-mocks (See files: compact-cards-v2.png, trace-sparkline.png).
- Backend queries: ENG draft SQLs are in the telemetry repo PR #842 (https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/842).
- API contract for sampling and trace snippets: https://api.redwood.ai/docs/console-telemetry-v1 (internal).

Rollout plan and communication:
- Phase 0 (internal): enable feature for Redwood internal orgs only, monitor telemetry for 72h.
- Phase 1 (beta): enable for 5 customer orgs that sign up for beta; coordinate success criteria with Solutions.
- Phase 2 (general): flip default for all orgs if Phase 1 acceptance is green.
- Release notes: add clear 'what's missing' section and link to roadmap for per-route drilldown.

Open questions and blockers:
- Do we need explicit legal approval for exposing cost deltas in email notifications? (Assign to Security/Legal for sign-off)
- Is there an infra quota risk from sampling bursts during incidents? ENG to validate with load tests.

Next steps (owner assigned):
- ENG: finalize short-form telemetry queries and add a staging dashboard (owner: Priya Suresh).
- Design: provide final compact-card assets and accessibility checks (owner: Mateo Chen).
- DOCS/Support: write the user-facing limitations and troubleshooting guide (owner: Lila Gomez).

This ticket bundles the scope-cut decisions so downstream teams have a single source of truth for what is included in the MVP and why. If we identify low-effort items that materially improve observability during Phase 0, we'll create follow-on PM tasks rather than reopen this ticket.

Alerts: email for cost deltas >20% including Console link
